subject: Money
title: Regulation After Crashes
description: Learn Regulation After Crashes in one minute.

hook.text: Glass-Steagall separated banks from casinos in 1933. It was repealed in 1999. The 2008 crash followed nine years later.

buildup.text: After every crash, new rules are written: SEC after 1929, Dodd-Frank after 2008, crypto regulations after 2022.

discovery.text: Regulations work—for a while. They prevent the exact same crisis from happening again in the exact same way.

twist.text: But innovation creates new loopholes. Shadow banking, DeFi, and SPACs all exploited gaps in existing rules.

climax.text: The pattern: crash, regulate, forget, deregulate, innovate around rules, crash again. Memory fades every 20 years.

punchline.text: We regulate the last crisis. Never the next one.

quiz.question: Why do financial regulations eventually fail to prevent new crises?
options: Innovation creates new products that exploit gaps in existing rules
